Community Choice Aggregator (CCA) and Regional Energy Network (REN). Flag to identify claims that had participation by a REN or CCA. For PAs who are a REN or CCA, this flag should be true for all claims.

Flag to identify participation in an area designated as a disadvantaged community by the California Environmental Protection Agency (census tract). This indicates a geographic Hard-to-Reach (HTR) condition. Contributes to Hard-to-Reach (HTR) eligibility. Disadvantaged community participant counts are included in the Participant table.
Flag used to identify whether a site is a master metered multifamily residence for electric.
Emerging Technology Program. Flag to identify that the measure is a product of an emerging techonology program.
Flag used to identify whether a site is a master metered multifamily residence for gas.

Indicates the claim is being reported as Hard to Reach. The claim must satisfy one of the valid Hard to Reach qualification pathways. Hard to Reach participant counts are included in the Participant table.
Flag to identify customers where the primary language spoken is other than English. Contributes to Hard-to-Reach (HTR) eligibility.

Flag to identify whether the Claim represents a True-Up for a Normalized Metered Energy Consumption (NMEC) project. Set it to true if the Claim reflects adjusted savings based on post-implementation performance data.

Flag to identify projects at businesses with 25 or fewer employees, or annual electric demand is less than 20 kW, or annual gas usage is less than 10,000 therms. Contributes to Hard-to-Reach (HTR) eligibility.
Flag to identify measures that are installed at locations that are leased or rented. Contributes to Hard-to-Reach (HTR) eligibility.
On Bill Financing. Flag to identify measures that had on-bill financing.

Flag to identify measures installed at customer premises located outside the United States Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Combined Statistical Areas of the San Francisco Bay Area, Greater Los Angeles Area, and Greater Sacramento Area, and outside the OMB metropolitan statistical area of San Diego County. This indicates a geographic Hard-to-Reach (HTR) condition. Contributes to HTR eligibility.
The claim is the final payment of a set of partial payments.
Public primary and secondary schools up to 12th grade. Flag to identify public K-12 schools
Flag to identify the residential customer meets the low-income definition through CARE or FERA eligibility. Contributes to Hard-to-Reach (HTR) eligibility.
Flag to identify residential multi-family homes and mobile/manufactured homes where tenants rent or lease the dwelling. Contributes to Hard-to-Reach (HTR) eligibility.
Flag to identify that claim was revised since it was originally submitted.
Flag to indentify program is in an underserved community.

Flag to identify Cultural Accessibility. It identifies California Native American Tribes as hard to reach. Tribal customers qualify independently under Commission policy and do not need to meet additional Hard-to-Reach (HTR) criteria.
Flag to identify Local Government customer. Contributes to Hard-to-Reach (HTR) eligibility.

The persistent record identifier that matches with a Claim.ClaimID. All values must start with the PA code and claim the year in the format PA-YYYY. Part of the ContactClaim table compound primary key - the ContactID and ClaimID in combination need to be unique.

The persistent record identifier that matches to the PII Contact table. All values must start with the PA code. Part of the ContactClaim table compound primary key - the ContactID and ClaimID in combination need to be unique.

The unique and persistent record identifier and the primary key for the Measure table. Must match the corresponding ClaimID in the Claim table. All values must start with the PA code and claim year in the format PA-YYYY. This field was previously called CEInputID.
The unique program identifier; joins to the ProgramCost table.
The year and quarter when the measure(s) were both installed and paid in e.g. '2023Q1'.
Measure-level sector aligned to the program business plan sectors.
From DEER. Identifies program implementation strategy/method of delivering a measure to a customer (e.g. direct install).
From DEER. Text codes that identify the building type/use and other parameters specific to that building use.  For example, 'Com' = Commercial buildings.

The geographic area where the installation is completed. The CEC designates micro-climate and ranges from 1 - 16. Use 'System' if a program or measure installation is not specific to an area or city. Required for cost effectiveness calc; Must be compatible with CET values (e.g. '3A').
Used to profile typical period of use for gas appliances/measures. Required for cost effectiveness calculation for measures with gas savings (e.g. 'Summer Only', 'Winter Only', 'Annual').
Used to determine how gas is purchased by the customer (e.g. 'Residential', 'Commercial', 'Core'). Required for cost effectiveness calculation for measures with gas savings.
Identifies the measure electric end use shape (i.e. load shape). Required for cost effectiveness calculation for measures with electric savings.
Identifies the sector being targeted by the measure intervention. Required for cost effectiveness calculation for measures with electric savings.
From DEER. The measure application identifies the context for the measure's installation. (e.g. accelerated replacement, new construction or behavioral).
PA-specific measure code.
Description of measure; should include enough information to allow understanding of what EE measure(s) being installed.
From DEER. Describes how the savings impact was determined (e.g. Deemed-DEER, Deemed-Workpaper, Site-specific calculation, etc.).

This field references a CEDARS value list used to identify fuel substitution for Deemed measures. FuelID distinguishes exempt and non-exempt Deemed measure packages under the Viable Electric Alternative (VEA) framework established in D.23-04-035.
Unique and persistent measure identifier.

From DEER. All Technology Types in an end use are associated with a high-level Technology Group. For example, in the 'lighting' end use all screw-in lighting technologies, including compact fluorescent lamps (CFLs), light-emitting diodes (LEDs), and incandescent lamps are part of a Technology Group. All hard-wired lighting fixtures are part of a different Technology Group.

From DEER. Technology Type is more specific than Technology Group. For example, a Technology Group can be further classified into individual parts. For example, all screw-in lighting technologies, including compact fluorescent lamps (CFLs), light-emitting diodes (LEDs), and incandescent lamps are included in the same Technology Group.
From DEER. Describes the end use of the measure in broad terms  (e.g. HVAC, lighting, motors, refrigeration, process).
From DEER. This is a more specific end use subcategory (e.g. the Lighting UseCategory contains Indoor General, Exit Signs, etc.).
Water Energy Calculator water used to calculate water energy savings.
Pre-existing measure description.
Standard measure description.

Type of normalizing units, or basis of NumUnits or quantity used by the cost effectiveness calculation (e.g. 'Lamp', 'hp', 'tons', 'facility', etc.).

Number of units or quantity. NumUnits must work in conjunction with the NormUnit value for the claim. Cross reference NormUnit and NumUnits before interpreting quantities of measures installed. This field is used in CEDARS cost and savings equations.
The first baseline kW Impact per Unit. This field is used in CEDARS savings equations.
The first baseline kWh Impact per Unit. This field is used in CEDARS savings equations.
The first baseline therm Impact per Unit. This field is used in CEDARS savings equations.

This field is the installed measure cost. Incremental Measure Cost or Full Measure Cost for the first baseline period, as appropriate for the MeasAppType and DeliveryType. Incremental measure cost over Code/Std for single baseline measures. This field is not used for dual baseline Cost effectiveness calculations, except when calculating excess incentives (for single and dual baseline measures). This field is used in CEDARS cost equations.

NPV gross measure cost based on first and second baseline measure costs. The Desktop CET called this field 'Gross Measure Cost_ER' (where ER = early retirement, aka accelerated replacement). This is the only measure cost field used for dual baseline CE calculations, except UnitMeaCost1stBaseline is used to calculate excess incentives (for single and dual baseline measures). This field is used in CEDARS cost equations.

This field is the actual cost in dollars of installation labor. Enter the unit incentive for labor. Cost effectiveness calculator uses this field; and overrides ExAnte values for deemed claims, and is one of two incentive fields for Direct Install. Only use if a direct install. This field is used in CEDARS cost equations.

This field is the actual cost in dollars of installation materials. Enter the unit incentive for materials. Cost effectiveness calculator uses this field; and overrides ExAnte values for deemed claims, and is one of two incentive fields for Direct Install. Only use if direct install. This field is used in CEDARS cost equations.

This field is the actual cost of rebates to the end user in dollars. Enter rebate to the customer for each unit of the measure. Cost effectiveness calculator uses this field, and overrides ExAnte values for deemed claims. Only use if downstream delivery type. This field is used in CEDARS cost equations.

This field is the actual cost in dollars of incentives to others besides the end user. Enter the incentive for others for each unit of measure. Cost effectiveness calculator uses this field; and overrides ExAnte values for deemed claims. Only use if midstream or upstream delivery type. Input should always be '0' for custom measures This field is used in CEDARS cost equations.
From DEER. The Ex Ante NTG_ID associated with the NTG values being claimed.

kW-specific NTG value. Usually, there is one NTG value entered for all NTGR fields. Developed through evaluation studies. NTG describes the free-ridership that may be occurring within energy efficiency programs. This field is used in CEDARS savings equations.

kWh-specific NTG value. Usually, there is one NTG value entered for all NTGR fields. Developed through evaluation studies. NTG describes the free-ridership that may be occurring within energy efficiency programs. This field is used in CEDARS savings equations.

Therm-specific NTG value. Usually, there is one NTG value entered for all NTGR fields. Developed through evaluation studies. NTG describes the free-ridership that may be occurring within energy efficiency programs. This field is used in CEDARS savings equations.

Cost-specific NTG value. Usually, there is one NTG value entered for all NTGR fields. Developed through evaluation studies. NTG describes the free-ridership that may be occurring within energy efficiency programs.
